title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1966-11-19

ai_review.summary: High‑energy early‑Dead show captured on a crisp soundboard tape, highlighted by Pigpen’s organ/vocals and standout blues‑rock numbers.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers a surprisingly clean mix for a 1966 soundboard source, letting the raw power of the band shine through. Reviewers rave about the blistering performances of “High Heeled Sneakers,” “Same Thing,” the “Smokestack > King Bee” medley and “Cream Puff War,” noting an especially fiery Pigpen presence and a bright, crystalline Jerry Garcia tone. Overall the show is described as a high‑octane snapshot of the Dead’s early garage‑blues era.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews are 4–5 stars and consistently praise both the performance and the tape quality, giving a clear consensus of an excellent early‑Dead show with good‑to‑excellent soundboard capture.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Most reviewers call the mix clean, crisp and impressive for a ’66 tape; a few note vintage tape limitations (mid‑range mud, modest fidelity) but no major dropouts.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑1966 setlist blends blues covers and original material; Pigpen’s organ/vocals dominate the middle, with tight transitions that keep momentum high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as having a crystalline, reverb‑tinged guitar tone that cuts through the mix.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass lines praised for their power and melodic interest; several reviewers mention “listening to Phil just for his lines.”
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming noted as driving and relentless, adding to the garage‑punk intensity.
